content: The files within ./QuantumInfo are not yet subjected to the same linters that ./Physlib are (and most of them would currently fail such linting). If anyone has spare capacity to help fix this (directly or via review) it would be great. As a start I have made Physlib#1212 which updates the linters so that they run on QuantumInfo by default, but then excludes them by inclusion in an exception file. Thus the essential goal is to the remove all the files from the exception file, as we get them to pass the linters.

If you have claude, I made this:

https://github.com/jstoobysmith/PhyslibAITools/blob/main/Scripts/auto-lint.sh

which is a script which does the complete workflow of forking, downloading, and making a pull-request to Physlib linting one of these files. If anyone has some time, I would appreciate a tester :)/ suggestions for improvements.

Arguably the dependencies should be installed by an AI assistant via a markdown instruction/prompt (along the line of SKILLS.md). Because currently the auto-install subset of the script excludes non-Debian distributions and Windows.
@Jinzheng Li made a user interface tool for this, which I think works on Windows too. But maybe in any case we should make a skill to download for Physlib and to make it easier for agents to use.

@Joseph Tooby-Smith
I just made a PR on PhyslibAiTool to publish GUI installers as v0.1.0 so people can directly download and use it.

Also, if the script is not working on your machine, what you can do is ask the AI assistant: “"run the auto-lint.sh and resolve any conflict for me"
